messages.title: Gold game plan — Thu 15 Oct
messages.text: Gold is digesting Wednesday's hot CPI: a ~2% drop from about 4,170 to a five-day low at 4,073, with Oct 28 hike odds up to ~42%. Retail sales and PPI at 6:00 PM IST are today's main volatility risk.
rows: Bearish structure below 4,150 (context, not a signal)
US retail sales + PPI, 8:30 AM ET = 6:00 PM IST
London 12:30 PM IST; NY overlap 5:30–9:30 PM IST, expect wide spreads near 6:00 PM
US 10-year near 5.2%, DXY reaction to PPI, Strait of Hormuz oil headlines

messages.text: Context from London. Headline CPI at 3.7% y/y was energy-heavy; core at 2.6% y/y is less alarming. If PPI confirms a hot pipeline, the hike gets priced further and real yields squeeze gold. A soft core PPI could spark a sharp short-covering bounce toward 4,150.
Asian range so far is 4,078 to 4,098. Yesterday's low at 4,073 sits just under it. That's an obvious sell-side pool for London to raid before we get any real direction.

messages.title: Saved lesson: the Asian range
messages.text: The Asian range is the high and low made roughly 5:30 AM to 12:30 PM IST. London often runs one side to collect stops before the real move. A raid only matters if price then displaces back through the range, leaving a fair value gap. Without displacement, a break is just a break.
Bias question: with the 10-year at 5.2%, why isn't gold already through 4,000? Feels like it should be weaker.

Because the haven bid hasn't gone anywhere. Hormuz risk, central bank buying and hedging against a policy mistake all support gold. High yields cap rallies; they don't automatically break support. That's why the plan says corrective bounces, not collapse.

messages.question: Your stance into today's PPI (6:00 PM IST)?

messages.text: Flat until the release for me. NY is my window anyway, and I'm not trying to front-run a print that can move gold 25 dollars in a minute.

London in 30 minutes. If we sweep 4,073 and M15 closes back inside the Asian range with displacement, that's the scenario I'm watching for a move toward 4,100+. If 4,050 breaks with acceptance, I stand aside.

messages.text: Screen recap: London swept the Asian low and yesterday's 4,073 low, tagged 4,056, then displaced up to 4,104. Now we're drifting 4,094-4,100 into the print. I'm not opening anything new before 6:00 PM.
Spreads already widening on my broker, 40+ cents. Anyone else?

Common before tier-one data. Wider spreads plus slippage can turn a 10-dollar stop into an effective 13-15. If you plan a position after the release, re-run the position size calculator with the wider stop, not this morning's.
Thinking of placing buy and sell stops 5 dollars either side right before 6. Easy money if it rips?

Jake, that often gets both sides filled in the first-second whipsaw, and slippage pushes each loss past your stop. Let the first 5-15 minutes print, then trade a retest of the impulse. You give up a bit of the move but keep your edge measurable.
Fair. Two stop-outs in one candle would hurt more than missing it.
Greetings from KL. What's your line in the sand after PPI?

4,050 below and 4,150 above. A hot PPI with acceptance under 4,050 opens 4,000. A soft PPI and a reclaim of 4,104 puts 4,150 in play, where I'd expect sellers again. Between those it's noise until proven otherwise.
Watching DXY alongside. If gold prints a new low after the release but DXY fails to make a new high, I'll log that SMT divergence in my journal.

Good habit. Pre-news reminders: 1) Know your max risk in dollars. 2) No orders resting at the print unless you accept slippage. 3) Decide invalidation before you see the candle. 4) If you feel rushed, the trade can wait.

rooms.name: ask-the-mentors
rooms.desc: Any question, beginner or advanced. Mentors and Goldie answer
rooms.pinned: Ask anything. Mentors and Goldie explain; nothing here is a signal.

messages.text: Advanced question: the London drop to 4,056, was that a liquidity sweep or genuine displacement lower? It broke yesterday's low cleanly on M15.

Judge it by what happened next. A sweep takes the pool and fails to hold beyond it: M15 closed back above 4,073 within two candles. Real displacement leaves an FVG and keeps going. Here the energetic candles were the ones back up, leaving an FVG at 4,074-4,081.

Checklist to separate them on M15: 1) Did price take an obvious pool, like the Asian or prior-day low? 2) Did a candle close back inside? 3) Was there a market structure shift with an FVG the other way? 4) Did it happen in a killzone? Today all four point to a sweep.
What's the difference between a mitigation block and a breaker block? I keep mixing them up.

Both are failed order blocks. A breaker forms when price first takes liquidity beyond a swing, then breaks structure the other way. A mitigation block fails without that liquidity grab, typically a lower high or higher low that gives way. Breakers tend to be the stronger reference.
How do real yields at 5.2% and a possible hike square with safe-haven demand? Textbook says gold should be far lower.

Real yields are the opportunity cost of holding gold, so hike repricing is a headwind. But haven demand responds to tail risk: Hormuz, fiscal worries, a Fed that may overtighten. With both live you get two-way trade: sharp drops on data, dip buying on headlines.
So the correlation with yields weakens rather than breaks?
Exactly. Track it on a rolling basis, not as a rule. When gold falls less than yields imply, that's haven demand absorbing supply. That has been the story since summer.
Is it better to fade a CPI spike or wait for the retest?

Fading the first spike bets the market misread the number, which is rare on a clean beat. Waiting for a retest of the impulse's FVG gives a defined stop and confirms the move held. Yesterday the retest into 4,142 was the cleaner trade than catching the drop.

rooms.name: chart-reviews
rooms.desc: Post a chart, get Goldie's checklist and mentor feedback
rooms.pinned: Post timeframe, entry, stop and target. Goldie reviews reasoning, not outcomes.

messages.text: First chart post, please be honest with me. M15 after the London sweep.
Long after London swept 4,056 and displaced up. Entering on the pullback, stop under the last small candle, target the 4,150 resistance before PPI.
Great job writing it out in full, Arjun. Here's my review of the reasoning, not a verdict on the trade.
checks: Context: the sweep of 4,073 and 4,056 plus displacement fits the London playbook
Location: 4,098 sits in premium of the 4,056-4,104 leg, not a discount PD array
Risk: a 5-dollar stop is under one M15 ATR (about 9) and too tight into PPI
Timing: a 4,150 target assumes the move survives a tier-one release
Plan: entry, stop and target were defined before posting

messages.text: Ouch, but fair. So where would a discount entry have been?

Try this: mark the 4,056 low to the 4,104 high and find equilibrium. Is your entry in premium or discount? Then ask where your idea is truly invalid, beyond the sweep or under a random candle? Your plan, your call.

Mentor feedback: your read was right, your location wasn't. Two fixes. Wait for price to return to discount instead of chasing. And size from the stop, not the other way round. A 1.5x ATR stop near 14 dollars means a smaller lot, and that's fine.
Got it. I'll post a revised plan after PPI, not before.
Saving this thread. The premium vs discount point finally clicked for me.
Worth remembering: 1% risk on a 10,000 account with a 14-dollar stop is about 0.07 lots. With a 5-dollar stop it's 0.20 lots, so each extra dollar of PPI slippage costs nearly three times as much.

Both can be right on different timeframes. Lukas is trading the H1 leg, Kelvin the H4 swing. The real question is which one PPI sides with.

Then I don't trade, which is a perfectly good outcome. Missing a move costs nothing. Shorting from the middle with the stop at the same high means more risk for the same target.

Useful contrast. Questions for both ideas: what would invalidate the bias before the stop is hit? How does each behave if PPI moves gold 30 dollars in a minute? Is the size calculated on the stop with slippage included?

rooms.name: pro-desk
rooms.desc: Pro and Mentor room for deeper market structure and risk discussion
rooms.pinned: Pro room. Assumes ICT/SMC fluency. Bring data, not vibes.

messages.text: SMT note from London: gold swept 4,073 down to 4,056 while DXY failed to make a higher high above its post-CPI peak. Lower low in gold, no confirmation in the dollar. That divergence was my confirmation before the MSS.
Respectful pushback: gold vs DXY SMT is noisier than correlated pairs like EURUSD vs GBPUSD. Yields and oil drive gold independently right now. I'd treat it as a secondary filter, never the trigger.

Both fair. I only use it as confluence inside a killzone at a known pool. Outside those, gold-DXY divergence is often just real-yield or oil noise. Today it lined up with the sweep, the time and the PD array, which is why it carried weight.
PPI sizing question. M15 ATR is around 9 now but hit 22 on the CPI candle. How do you size a post-release trade?

One approach: use post-release ATR, not pre-news. If the first M15 after the print ranges 22 dollars, a 1.5x ATR stop is about 33. At 0.5% risk on 50,000, that's 250 dollars, about 0.075 lots, rounded down to 0.07 in the calculator. Wider stop, smaller size, same risk.
I prefer halving risk for the first hour after tier-one data instead of widening to 1.5x ATR. Same principle, simpler to execute when the tape is moving fast.
Journaling question. Last 60 trades: 38% win rate, average win 2.6R, average loss 0.9R. Yet it feels like I'm losing. Is the math lying?

The math is fine: 0.38 x 2.6 minus 0.62 x 0.9 is about +0.43R per trade. It feels bad because 62% of trades are red. Track expectancy and max consecutive losses; at 38%, a run of 6-8 losers is normal variance, not a broken system.
On trailing vs fixed TP: in this regime I bank a partial at the opposing liquidity, then trail the rest under M15 swing lows. Pure trailing gave back too much in the chop since CPI.

Agreed. Trailing pays in trending, expanding markets. We're in a two-way, event-driven range around 4,050-4,150 until the 28th, so fixed targets at the opposite pool fit better. Revisit once price breaks and accepts outside it.
On losing streaks: after three consecutive losses I halve size and only take A+ setups for the rest of the week. It stops the revenge spiral without pretending the edge has disappeared.

A simple reset routine: 1) Sort recent losses into rule breaks vs normal variance. 2) Reduce risk until you're back at baseline. 3) Write the next trade's plan before opening charts. Losses inside the plan are a business cost; rule breaks are the real fix.
